about: The physics a hex run takes when it names none, on every door (forecast, global, zoom globe, regions, country, storm-following, ensembles, cycles, Hex with Regional parents, DA backgrounds). Owner ruling 2026-10-25: 'now that mpas physics are good those should be the default in general and on site'. The default is MPAS-A v8.4.2's own physics on the MPAS route, the suite chosen by the mesh's finest cell spacing from the rules below (first match). ArWen physics stays selectable: --physics-suite arwen_mpas_column (or any hex suite, a --physics KEY=VALUE override, an explicit --convection or --physics-backend row) takes the ArWen route exactly as a bare run did before 0.4.6.

rules.why: MPAS-A v8.4 user's guide (Physics Suites): convection_permitting is the recommended suite where convection-permitting cells (dx < 10 km) are used, including variable-resolution meshes spanning hydrostatic to nonhydrostatic scales; mesoscale_reference is not appropriate at convective scales (New Tiedtke suppresses instability before resolved cells respond). Regions, zoom globes, storm-following members and every variable-resolution mesh with a fine core land here.

Quasi-uniform meshes of 10 km and coarser. MPAS-A's Registry default for them is mesoscale_reference (tested above 10 km), and convection_permitting is also MPAS-A practice there: the guide says it was tested from several hundred kilometres down to 3 km, its Grell-Freitas scheme being scale-aware. hex takes convection_permitting because it is the suite that runs entirely on the GPU in this release (mesoscale_reference's MPAS interface glue is not ported yet and is refused by name: hexcore.mpasphys.resident_v842.ported_route_refusal), it is the suite proven bitwise to native MPAS-A (hl-3) and within 1.2x of the ArWen route on every shape, and on 2025-05-19 it showed no wet bias where the ArWen route was about 2x too wet. When mesoscale_reference runs on the GPU, switching coarse meshes to it is this row, decided by obs skill.
